events.comment: Shared combat rules. Runs before the Samurai events so they can react on the same frame.
Tutorial scene start: play this scene's music.
Samurai: position the enemy bars above it.
Samurai: stay idle once the player is deleted.
Samurai: posture broke, so cancel its attack, including any wall slash or dash strike that has not landed yet.
Samurai: stun ended or deathblow landed, so go back to chasing.
Samurai: a lunge landed, so cancel whatever he is doing and flinch. A posture break, lost life or death from the same hit takes priority.
Samurai: the stagger ended, so go back to chasing.
Samurai: count deflects during his swing combo. The third one plays the sword clash on top of the parry sound.
Third deflect of the combo: play the clash and start counting again.
Samurai recoil after a lunge stagger: slide away from the player for RecoilTime seconds, at RecoilSpeed.
Player on the right: slide left.
Player on the left: slide right.
Samurai: play its hit sound when it hits the player.
Stun: pause on the kneeling frame.
Stun: after KneelHold seconds, play the get-up frames.
Boss: final death. Play Samurai_Death, with two holds handled below, and leave the body on its last frame.
Death: pause on the settled kneeling frame, before he reaches for the blade.
Death: after DeathKneelHold seconds, carry on with the seppuku.
Death: pause with the blade drawn in, before he collapses.
Death: after DeathCutHold seconds, play the collapse.
Boss: lost a life, so start the intermission. Physics stay off during the taller petal animations, so the boss does not jump upward.

Boss: at 75%, 50% and 25% HP on the last life, cast the ultimate. UltHpStep sets the HP gap and UltMaxCasts the number of casts. A hit that crosses two marks only triggers one cast. Locks the player, removes attacks still in flight, and starts the petal teleport instead of the cut.
Boss: dodged a hit. The first dodge of the fight always goes behind the player, later ones are random.
Boss: the player swings nearby, so maybe dodge that hit. DodgeChance and DodgeDelay control this. He cannot dodge during a stagger.
Boss: a lunge is coming in, so check once per lunge whether to dodge it. It starts too far away for the check above, which only runs on an attack press.
Same rules as a swing: DodgeChance and DodgeDelay control this.
Boss offense: every GrabCooldown seconds, with the player within GrabTriggerRange, flash step behind them for the grab.
Boss offense: when the cooldown is ready and the player is far away, roll a new cooldown. On a successful roll, flash the eye glint before the dash strike. Otherwise keep walking.
Boss offense: the eye glint finished, so start the dash strike.
Aggressive phase, player at range: choose a skill.
Aggressive phase, player close: dash away, then choose a skill.
Aggressive phase: pick a Judgement Cut or the tornado at random. Two cuts in a row guarantee a tornado next.
Combo: sometimes go to the far wall first, then cast the tornado and follow it with a dash.

Flash step: halfway through vanishing, teleport and draw the trail, then face the player. The dash strike passes through the player and faces away. If a wall leaves no room, it lands in front and uses the crescent slash.
Grab: land close behind the player, on the side they are not facing.
Flash step finished: counter after going behind. After a dash away in the aggressive phase, choose a skill. After the combo dash, cast the tornado.
Grab: he has landed. Show the warning kanji over his head and start the tell, with the eye glint.
Grab tell: he can be hit here, and a posture break cancels the grab. Keep the kanji over his head and keep facing the player.
Keep the warning kanji centered above his head while it exists.
Remove the kanji if the grab was interrupted, by a stun, dodge, ultimate or debug key.
Grab tell over: lunge with both hands. Only a dodge or distance beats this, because the grab skips the deflect check.
Grab connects: the player is within GrabRange and not rolling or invulnerable. He seizes them, and both play their grab animations.
Turn the player to face him, so they fall away from him.
Grab missed: he is left over-reached for GrabWhiffTime seconds, which is the punish window.
Grab missed: recover and go back to chasing.
Grab: yank the player in to GrabHoldDist from him before the stab.

parameters: (Samurai_NPC.CenterX() + sign(Player.CenterX() - Samurai_NPC.CenterX()) * Samurai_NPC.Variable(GrabHoldDist) - Player.CenterX()) * min(1, 25 * TimeDelta())

events.comment: Grab: the blade goes in. GrabDamage applies directly here, so the deflect check never sees it. The HP can be rallied back like any other hit.
Grab: he rips the blade out.
Grab: the player hits the ground.
Grab over: the player has got up, so free them and go back to chasing.
Wall slash: the boss can be hit once the arrival streak ends. The stance and sword glint are the punish window.
Dash strike: spawn a hidden hitbox covering only the slash line, not his body.
Wall slash: spawn a hidden hitbox covering only the crescent, on the frames where it appears.
Dash strike finished: go back to chasing and start the dash cooldown from now.
Wall slash finished: go back to chasing and start the dash cooldown from now.
Dash strike: remove the line hitbox once the slash has faded.
Wall slash: remove the crescent hitbox when the crescent fades.
Dash strike and wall slash: remove the hidden hitbox if the attack was interrupted.
Quickdraw: on the draw frame, cut at the player position with a random variation.
Quickdraw finished: go back to chasing.
Tornado: on the release frame, send it the way the boss is facing (right).
Tornado: on the release frame, send it the way the boss is facing (left).
Tornado cast finished: go back to chasing. In the combo, flash the eye glint and follow up with the dash strike.
Intermission: the petal burst ended, so hide and start the cuts.
Intermission: launch a cut at the player every 1.2 seconds.
Intermission: all cuts finished, so reappear on the far side and switch to the aggressive phase.
Intermission finished: switch back to a normal-height animation, turn platformer physics back on, and start chasing.
Ultimate teleport: the Samurai has dissolved into petals, so the player does too. The petals are sized and placed on the player: 32 is the height of the anchor above the feet in the petal art.
Ultimate teleport: fade the player out inside the petals, at UltFadeSpeed.
Ultimate teleport: both are gone, so move them to mid-arena. The Samurai keeps the side he was on, UltStandoff away from the player. UltCenterX is the arena middle.
Ultimate teleport: start the player petals so both finish reforming together. They are sized and placed on the player, like the dissolve.
Ultimate teleport: fade the player back in as the petals close up.
Ultimate teleport: both have reformed, so make sure the player is fully visible, bring back the bars, turn physics back on, and start the draw.
Ultimate: on the draw frame, cast Thousand Cuts on the player.
Ultimate finished: unlock the player and go back to the aggressive phase.
Ultimate: allow a new hit between slashes. Slashes land on frames 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31, and 34. Uses mod() because GDevelop expressions have no % operator.
Move the tornado along the ground.
Tornado: loop its full-size frames while it crosses the arena.
Tornado: near the left edge, start the fade so it finishes at the wall.
Tornado: near the right edge, start the fade so it finishes at the wall.
Remove a Judgement Cut when its animation ends.
Remove the tornado when its animation ends.
Remove the ultimate when its animation ends.
Ultimate effect: the scenery goes grey except inside the cut, fading in and out. Ground_Stuff is on the Background layer so it greys too, while the player and samurai stay in color.

inlineCode: // Ultimate effect: turns the Background layer grey, except for a colored circle at the cut.
const ULT_RADIUS = 198; // Circle radius in the image (66) times the object scale (3).
state = runtimeScene.__ultGrey = { amount: 0, flash: 0, lastFrame: -1, x: 0, y: 0, radius: 0, filter: null };
"precision highp float; // Must match the default vertex shader, or the shader fails and the layer disappears.",
"  float outside = smoothstep(uRadius - 3.0, uRadius + 3.0, distance(position, uCenter));",
state.filter = new PIXI.Filter(undefined, fragment, { uCenter: new Float32Array(2), uRadius: 0, uAmount: 0, uFlash: 0 });

events.comment: Remove the dash trail after 0.2 seconds.
Samurai_Idle Rules
Samurai_Waiting Rules
Samurai_AggroReady Rules
Close enough: start attacking. AttackRange is the same distance the follow-up check uses after each swing.
Samurai_Attacking Rules
First swing of a combo: start the deflect count over.
Swing: hold the raised sword for SwingPause seconds. The wait is the same every swing, so the rhythm can be learned.
Swing: after SwingPause seconds, release the sword and create the hitbox.

Swing finished, combo not over: if the player is behind the samurai or out of AttackRange, skip the next swing and go back to AggroReady to close the gap. ComboCount is kept, so the 3-swing limit still leads to Cooldown.
Samurai_Cooldown
Debug: F7 cancels whatever the Samurai is doing and casts the tornado at the player. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release.
Debug: F8 cancels whatever the Samurai is doing and starts the grab. Ignored during a stun, death, intermission, ultimate or grab. Remove before release.
